sonnet.problem: The question says "Instead of caring for the flock," which rules out the wrong answers "protects" and "fattens", since both are caring acts. That leaves "devours" as the only fit, so the setup gives the answer away.
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: The card tells the shepherd's actions in the present tense: "The shepherd the LORD raises up even tears off the hooves of the choice sheep." In verse 16 this is a prediction ("I will raise up a shepherd... he will devour... and tear off their hooves"). It should stay a prediction.
sonnet.rule: A prediction stays a prediction: "God says Tyre will fall," never "Tyre falls."

sonnet.problem: The question calls him "the worthless shepherd" under a woe. That makes the wrong answers "He guards the flock day and night" and "He leads the flock back home" implausible, so they aren't believable alternatives and the setup rules them out.
sonnet.rule: For why and meaning questions, wrong answers only need to be believable.
